question: What total amount of financing commitments and capacity backstops to customers and partners will NVIDIA report outstanding at its FY2027 year-end?

candidates.summary: The Information's prior reporting, relayed in the item, said NVIDIA has recently been negotiating to provide financial guarantees for OpenAI's lease of a large data center in Ohio — an asset that, if fully built out at current prices for chips, labor, power and other materials, could cost as much as $500 billion. The guarantee is described as under negotiation, not signed.

question: What dollar amount of NVIDIA supply and purchase commitments will its FY2027 Form 10-K disclose?
Will NVIDIA make first shipments of the Kyber NVL144 / Rubin Ultra rack platform during calendar 2027, as confirmed by NVIDIA or reported by SemiAnalysis?

candidates.summary: Research firm SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture — the cabinet designed to house 2027 Rubin Ultra chips, packing 144 GPUs per unit — has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, because the specialized multi-layer PCB midplane that connects the system's modules remains challenging from a manufacturability standpoint. The design had been slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027. Nvidia rejected the report (see separate item).
Nvidia rejected SemiAnalysis's report that its Kyber rack-scale architecture has been delayed, stating that its roadmap is intact.
SemiAnalysis said NVL576 — a larger system that links eight racks via optical connections, part of the Rubin Ultra lineup — is also likely delayed or limited to small volumes.

SemiAnalysis said a backup plan to expand Rubin Ultra's scale-up world size by bolting two of Nvidia's current-generation racks together for similar power has been cancelled, after cloud service providers and hyperscalers pushed back over its odd design and heavy operational burden.

SemiAnalysis said the delays leave Nvidia with 'no proven solution to expand the scale-up world size for Rubin Ultra,' predicting that this could give rivals Advanced Micro Devices and Google — whose in-house chips are already winning business from top AI labs — a rare technical opening at the high end of the market.

Research firm SemiAnalysis claimed that Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 high-density rack architecture — the design showcased at GTC earlier this year and built for Rubin Ultra GPUs — has slipped by more than 12 months, blaming persistent manufacturing problems with the system's complex PCB midplane. The item frames this as an allegation (reported delays into 2028) that Nvidia contests; no confirmed ship date is given.
